answer: I'd like to talk about something that is still a long way off for me, but which I think about quite often. Something I would genuinely love to own one day is a house of my own, ideally with a small garden. I picture a modest two-storey house on the edge of Sirajganj, not far from the river, with a few mango trees and space for my mother to grow vegetables. Right now it feels like a distant dream, but it is one I am steadily working towards. The main reason I want it is the sense of security and [[permanence]] that comes with owning your own home. We live in a comfortable flat on the third floor, but I've always longed for a [[patch of land]] of our own, something I only really enjoy when we visit my grandparents in the village. A home of my own would be a real [[sanctuary]], and a place where my father could enjoy his retirement surrounded by greenery. As for how I'd get it, I plan to save carefully over the coming years, which will require patience and [[discipline]]. I'll probably need a home loan as well, and I hope that gaining more experience, perhaps even studying abroad, will eventually improve my earnings. I imagine the feeling of finally getting the keys would be absolutely [[exhilarating]], a real milestone. It represents stability, achievement and a place to build a future. Honestly, I think there is something deeply satisfying about having a space that is truly yours. While I know it is a long-term goal that will take considerable effort, it is one I am determined to reach. It keeps me motivated to work hard and save wisely.

followUps.q: Do you think you will achieve this goal?
followUps.answer: I hope so, although realistically it will take quite a few years. As long as I stay disciplined with my savings and keep progressing in my career, I think it's an [[attainable]] goal.

followUps.q: Would you prefer to live in a house or a flat?
followUps.answer: A house, ideally. Flats are practical and secure, but I've always loved open space, fresh air and the idea of stepping out into my own garden with a morning cup of tea.
